name: Availability Heuristic
description: People judge how likely/relevant something is by how easily examples come to mind.
detection_hint: Does the page rely on abstract claims with no easy-to-picture scenario for when the product is needed?
example_fix: Add a concrete, relatable use-case scenario early in the copy.

name: Overconfidence
description: People overestimate their own knowledge or ability, which reduces perceived need for help.
detection_hint: Does copy assume the visitor already recognizes the problem, with no challenge to that assumption?
example_fix: Add a quick self-check/quiz that reveals a gap the visitor didn't expect.

name: Bystander Effect
description: Presence of many others reduces an individual's felt responsibility to act.
detection_hint: Is the CTA generic and impersonal rather than addressed to the individual visitor?
example_fix: Personalize CTA copy directly to the visitor ("Your plan", "Start yours").

name: Curiosity
description: Information gaps create a drive to seek closure, increasing engagement.
detection_hint: Do headlines fully reveal the content with no open question or gap?
example_fix: Use a curiosity-gap headline that teases the payoff without giving it away.

name: Facial Distraction
description: Human faces strongly pull visual attention, for better or worse.
detection_hint: Is a hero-image face looking away from the CTA or key info?
example_fix: Orient the model's gaze/face toward the CTA or product.

name: Gaze Cueing Effect
description: Viewers instinctively follow the gaze direction of a pictured person.
detection_hint: Is the pictured person looking off-page instead of toward key content?
example_fix: Reframe or select imagery where gaze points at the CTA/offer.

name: Inattentional Blindness Effect
description: Users can completely miss elements outside their focused attention path.
detection_hint: Is important information placed outside the natural scan path (e.g. sidebar, footer)?
example_fix: Move critical info into the primary F-pattern reading zone.

name: Joy and Fun
description: Positive affect increases engagement and receptivity to messaging.
detection_hint: Is the tone purely functional/dry with no moments of delight?
example_fix: Add small playful touches in microcopy or visuals where appropriate.

name: Picture Superiority Effect
description: Images are remembered significantly better than text alone.
detection_hint: Is a key benefit explained only in text with no supporting visual?
example_fix: Illustrate the key benefit with an image, icon, or diagram.

name: Salience
description: Visually prominent elements draw disproportionate attention.
detection_hint: Does the CTA visually compete with other high-contrast elements on the page?
example_fix: Increase contrast/size of the primary CTA and reduce competing visual noise.

name: Streisand Effect
description: Trying to hide information tends to draw more attention to it.
detection_hint: Is negative info (fees, limitations) awkwardly buried or hidden?
example_fix: Address known objections openly instead of concealing them.

name: Vampire Effect
description: An overly attention-grabbing element steals focus from the actual message.
detection_hint: Does the hero visual outshine or distract from the offer/CTA?
example_fix: Simplify or mute visuals that compete with the core message.

name: Barnum Effect
description: Vague, general statements feel personally relevant to almost everyone.
detection_hint: Are benefit claims generic ("perfect for everyone") rather than specific?
example_fix: Write segment-specific benefit statements instead of universal claims.

name: Empathy Gap
description: People underestimate how much future emotional states will drive their decisions.
detection_hint: Is there no framing of the emotional payoff after using the product?
example_fix: Describe the post-purchase emotional relief or satisfaction explicitly.

name: Focusing Effect
description: Overweighting one prominent attribute while ignoring other relevant ones.
detection_hint: Does one benefit dominate messaging while other real benefits are invisible?
example_fix: Balance the headline benefit with 2-3 supporting secondary benefits.

name: FOMO
description: Fear of missing out drives faster action.
detection_hint: Are there no urgency, scarcity, or social-activity signals present?
example_fix: Add a genuine limited-time or limited-availability signal.

name: Funktionale Fixierung
description: Difficulty seeing alternative uses or contexts for a product.
detection_hint: Does copy show only one narrow use-case for the product?
example_fix: Show multiple use-cases or contexts where the product applies.

name: Identifiable Victim Effect
description: People respond more strongly to one specific person's story than to statistics.
detection_hint: Are only aggregate stats shown with no individual story?
example_fix: Add a named customer story alongside the statistic.

name: Inaction Inertia Effect
description: Missing a past good deal makes people less likely to act on a current, lesser one.
detection_hint: Is a returning visitor shown the same or worse offer than one they previously skipped?
example_fix: Give returning visitors who abandoned a fresh, distinct incentive.

name: Status Quo Bias
description: People prefer to keep things as they are and resist change.
detection_hint: Is there no explicit contrast between acting now vs. doing nothing?
example_fix: Frame the cost of staying with the current situation explicitly.

name: Threat
description: A perceived risk or threat increases motivation to act.
detection_hint: Is there no honest framing of the risk of not acting?
example_fix: Name the real, factual risk of inaction without exaggeration.

name: Context Dependent Memory
description: Recall is stronger when the current context matches the context of first exposure.
detection_hint: Does the landing page look visually inconsistent with the ad that drove the click?
example_fix: Match landing page visuals/copy closely to the originating ad creative.

name: Primacy Effect
description: The first items presented in a sequence are remembered best.
detection_hint: Is the weakest selling point listed first?
example_fix: Lead with the single strongest benefit or argument.

name: Recency Effect
description: The last items presented in a sequence are remembered best.
detection_hint: Does a page or section end on a weak or flat note?
example_fix: Close sections and pages with a strong, memorable statement.

name: Recognition over Recall Effect
description: Recognizing something is cognitively easier than recalling it from memory.
detection_hint: Does the flow force users to remember past choices instead of showing them?
example_fix: Show recently viewed or saved items instead of asking users to recall them.

name: Rhyme-as-Reason Effect
description: Statements that rhyme or have rhythm are judged as more credible.
detection_hint: Is there no memorable, rhythmic phrasing for the core value proposition?
example_fix: Craft a short, rhythmic tagline for the core claim.

name: Rosy Retrospection
description: Past experiences are remembered more positively than they actually were.
detection_hint: Is a returning customer's past experience not referenced at all?
example_fix: Reference the customer's positive past experience ("Welcome back").

name: Serial Position Effect
description: Items at the start and end of a list are remembered best; middle items are forgotten.
detection_hint: Is the recommended plan/option placed in the middle of a list?
example_fix: Place the recommended option first or last in the list.

name: Story Bias
description: Narratives are more persuasive and memorable than raw facts alone.
detection_hint: Is the page a pure feature/spec list with no narrative thread?
example_fix: Wrap key facts into a short customer story or scenario.

name: Von Restorff Effect
description: An item that visually stands out from its surroundings is remembered better.
detection_hint: Is the recommended plan visually identical to the other options?
example_fix: Visually highlight the recommended option (color, badge, size).

name: Affektheuristik
description: Decisions are guided by current emotional state rather than pure analysis.
detection_hint: Is the copy purely technical/rational with no emotional register at all?
example_fix: Add emotionally resonant language alongside the factual claims.

name: Ambiguity Aversion
description: People prefer a known risk over an unknown, unclear one.
detection_hint: Are terms left vague (e.g. "flexible cancellation" with no specifics)?
example_fix: State exact terms and numbers instead of vague qualifiers.

name: Authenticity
description: Perceived genuineness increases trust in the source.
detection_hint: Is the page overly polished with generic stock photography?
example_fix: Use real photos of the team, product, or customers.

name: Authority
description: Credentialed or expert sources are more persuasive.
detection_hint: Are claims made with no expert or credential backing nearby?
example_fix: Attribute key claims to a credentialed expert, certification, or standard.

name: Bandwagon Effect
description: People are more likely to do what they see many others doing.
detection_hint: Is there no indication of how many people already use the product?
example_fix: Show adoption numbers or a "most popular" label.

name: Cheerleader Effect
description: Items appear more appealing when shown in a group than alone.
detection_hint: Is the product shown only in an isolated, out-of-context shot?
example_fix: Show the product alongside complementary items or in real-life context.

name: Equality Attraction
description: People trust and like others they perceive as similar to themselves.
detection_hint: Does imagery/testimonial selection fail to reflect the target audience?
example_fix: Use imagery and testimonials that visibly match the target segment.

name: In-Group Bias
description: People favor members of groups they identify with.
detection_hint: Is messaging generic rather than tailored to a specific customer segment?
example_fix: Tailor copy and imagery to the specific segment being addressed.

name: Liking
description: People are more easily persuaded by sources they like.
detection_hint: Is the copywriting tone cold or impersonal?
example_fix: Rewrite in a warmer, more personable voice.

name: Mere Exposure Effect
description: Repeated exposure to something increases preference for it.
detection_hint: Does the brand/product appear only once across the whole funnel?
example_fix: Reinforce brand presence across multiple touchpoints (retargeting, repetition).

name: Pratfall Effect
description: An otherwise competent source admitting a minor flaw increases likability and trust.
detection_hint: Are all claims presented as flawless with zero acknowledged limitation?
example_fix: Acknowledge one honest limitation alongside the strengths.

name: Smalltalk-Technik
description: A light, informal exchange before the main ask builds rapport.
detection_hint: Does the flow go straight into a hard sell with no rapport step?
example_fix: Add a light, low-stakes interaction (quiz, preference question) before the ask.

name: Social Proof
description: People look to others' actions, especially similar others, to guide their own.
detection_hint: Are reviews, ratings, or usage stats absent near the decision point?
example_fix: Add reviews, ratings, or "X people chose this" near the CTA.

name: Trust Bias
description: People are predisposed to trust familiar-looking or consistently branded elements.
detection_hint: Does checkout branding look inconsistent with the rest of the site?
example_fix: Keep branding visually consistent all the way through checkout.

name: Uncanny Valley Effect
description: Near-human but imperfect representations feel unsettling and reduce trust.
detection_hint: Is a synthetic avatar or AI voice used in a way that feels almost-but-not-quite human?
example_fix: Use clearly human or clearly abstract representations, avoiding the near-human middle ground.

name: Aesthetics Heuristic
description: Attractive design is unconsciously assumed to signal better function ("what is beautiful is good").
detection_hint: Is the visual design dated or inconsistent?
example_fix: Invest in polished, modern, consistent visual design.

name: Curse of Knowledge
description: Experts struggle to imagine what a novice doesn't already know, leading to jargon.
detection_hint: Is copy full of unexplained jargon or internal terminology?
example_fix: Rewrite key copy in plain language a first-time visitor would understand.

name: Decoy Effect
description: Adding a third, deliberately inferior option makes one of the other two more attractive.
detection_hint: Are only two pricing options offered?
example_fix: Add a third, less-attractive tier that steers choice toward the target plan.

name: Dilution Effect
description: Irrelevant information weakens the impact of the relevant information around it.
detection_hint: Is the key benefit buried among unrelated details?
example_fix: Remove irrelevant details from the immediate vicinity of the key benefit/CTA.

name: Extremeness Aversion
description: People tend to avoid extreme options, preferring the middle choice.
detection_hint: Is there no clearly positioned "middle" option among the choices?
example_fix: Position the target plan as the visually and logically middle option.

name: Framing
description: Presenting the same fact as a gain or a loss changes its perceived value.
detection_hint: Is a benefit stated only in gain terms (or only in loss terms), unexamined?
example_fix: A/B test gain-framed vs. loss-framed copy for the same underlying fact.

name: Having vs. Using Effect
description: Focusing on the experience of use is more persuasive than focusing on mere ownership.
detection_hint: Does copy emphasize "get/own" rather than the experience of using it?
example_fix: Describe the day-to-day experience of using the product, not just owning it.

name: Inner Dialogue
description: Prompting a visitor's self-reflective inner dialogue increases engagement.
detection_hint: Are there no reflective or rhetorical questions posed to the visitor?
example_fix: Add a rhetorical question inviting self-reflection ("Tired of X?").

name: Negativity Bias
description: Negative information weighs more heavily than positive information of equal size.
detection_hint: Are negative reviews or common complaints left unaddressed nearby?
example_fix: Proactively and honestly address common objections near the decision point.

name: Neomanie
description: A general preference for what is new over what is established.
detection_hint: Are new or updated features not signaled as "new"?
example_fix: Explicitly highlight new or recently updated aspects of the product.

name: Noble Edge Effect
description: Companies seen as ethical or socially responsible are preferred, even at a premium.
detection_hint: Is there no visibility of sustainability or ethical practices?
example_fix: Surface genuine ethical/sustainability credentials near the decision point.

name: Not-Invented-Here Syndrome
description: Resistance to solutions the user did not have a hand in creating.
detection_hint: Is the offering rigid with zero customization or configuration?
example_fix: Allow some personalization/configuration so users feel ownership.

name: Paradox of Choice
description: Too many options reduce satisfaction and increase decision paralysis.
detection_hint: Is there a long list of similar plans/options with no guidance on which to pick?
example_fix: Reduce the number of options or add a clearly marked recommended default.

name: Price-Quality-Illusion
description: A higher price is unconsciously assumed to signal higher quality.
detection_hint: Is the lowest-price option the most visually prominent, unintentionally signaling "cheap = worse"?
example_fix: Reconsider visual hierarchy so price doesn't unintentionally signal low quality.

name: Time vs. Money Effect
description: Framing benefits in terms of time saved can be more persuasive than money saved.
detection_hint: Is only monetary savings mentioned, with no time-saved framing?
example_fix: Add a time-saved framing alongside any monetary framing.

name: WYSIATI Effect
description: People judge based only on visible information, ignoring what's missing ("what you see is all there is").
detection_hint: Is important missing information (e.g. hidden fees) simply left out, relying on it not being noticed?
example_fix: Surface all relevant information explicitly rather than relying on omission.

name: Anchoring
description: The first number seen strongly influences subsequent judgments of value.
detection_hint: Is there no reference or strikethrough price shown before the actual price?
example_fix: Show a higher reference price before revealing the discounted price.

name: Charm Price Effect
description: Prices ending in .99/.90 are perceived as meaningfully cheaper than round numbers.
detection_hint: Is pricing shown as a round number (e.g. CHF 30.00)?
example_fix: Test charm pricing (CHF 29.90) against round pricing.

name: External Reference
description: Comparing price to an external, related benchmark increases perceived value.
detection_hint: Is there no comparison to an alternative or competing cost?
example_fix: Add a price comparison to a relevant external benchmark.

name: House Money Effect
description: Money already saved or won is spent more freely than money earned.
detection_hint: Is a prior saving/credit not reminded to the user before an upsell?
example_fix: Remind users of savings or credit already accrued right before an upsell.

name: Magnitude Priming
description: Exposure to a large number makes a subsequent smaller number feel smaller still.
detection_hint: Is the price shown with no larger number shown beforehand?
example_fix: Show total annual or lifetime value before revealing the smaller monthly price.

name: Money Illusion
description: People evaluate nominal prices rather than real, adjusted value.
detection_hint: Is there no context provided for whether a price is objectively good value?
example_fix: Add a per-unit or per-day cost breakdown for context.

name: Pennies-a-day Effect
description: Breaking a price into small daily units makes it feel cheaper.
detection_hint: Is only the total price shown, with no per-day breakdown?
example_fix: Show the price broken into a "per day" figure alongside the total.

name: Precision Heuristic
description: Precise numbers feel more calculated and trustworthy than round ones.
detection_hint: Is pricing round and seemingly arbitrary (e.g. CHF 50.00)?
example_fix: Use precise pricing where it genuinely reflects a real calculation.

name: Rule of Hundred
description: Below CHF 100, percentage discounts feel bigger; above CHF 100, absolute discounts feel bigger.
detection_hint: Is the discount framing (% vs absolute) mismatched to the price magnitude?
example_fix: Use % discounts under CHF 100 and absolute CHF discounts above CHF 100.

name: Zero Price Effect
description: "Free" is disproportionately more attractive than a small price, beyond its rational value.
detection_hint: Is there no free trial or free tier offered where one could feasibly exist?
example_fix: Offer a genuinely free entry tier or trial instead of a token low price.

name: Zero Risk Bias
description: People overvalue completely eliminating a small risk versus reducing a larger one.
detection_hint: Is there no explicit guarantee that fully eliminates purchase risk?
example_fix: Offer and emphasize a guarantee that removes risk entirely, not just reduces it.

name: Base Rate Fallacy
description: People ignore general statistical likelihood in favor of vivid, specific information.
detection_hint: Does the page rely on an anecdote with no supporting base-rate statistic?
example_fix: Pair a vivid testimonial with a supporting statistic.

name: Black-and-White Fallacy
description: Presenting only two extreme options when more nuance genuinely exists.
detection_hint: Is the choice framed as a false binary ("do this or fail")?
example_fix: Only use binary framing where genuinely true; otherwise show the real nuance.

name: Disrupt-then-Reframe
description: Breaking an expected pattern makes the audience more receptive to what follows.
detection_hint: Is the offer structure entirely predictable with no pattern break?
example_fix: Open with an unexpected framing before presenting the standard offer.

name: Door-in-the-Face-Technik
description: Starting with a large request makes a smaller, real request seem reasonable by comparison.
detection_hint: Is only one plan/ask shown, with no higher anchor option first?
example_fix: Present a premium option first, then the target plan as the reasonable choice.

name: Evoking Freedom
description: Explicitly affirming the user's freedom to choose or decline reduces resistance.
detection_hint: Is the language pushy or freedom-limiting ("You must...")?
example_fix: Add explicit language affirming choice ("cancel anytime", "no obligation").

name: False Consensus
description: People overestimate how much others share their views or choices.
detection_hint: Is there no signal of how common a given choice actually is?
example_fix: Show adoption stats reinforcing that the choice is common.

name: Foot-in-the-Door-Technik
description: Agreeing to a small request first increases compliance with a larger request later.
detection_hint: Does the funnel jump straight to full commitment with no small first step?
example_fix: Add a small, low-commitment first step (email signup, free tool) before the full ask.

name: Hyperbolic Discounting
description: People overvalue immediate rewards relative to larger future rewards.
detection_hint: Is only long-term value highlighted, with no immediate benefit called out?
example_fix: Highlight an immediate benefit alongside the long-term value.

name: Mere Agreement
description: Small verbal or written agreements increase the likelihood of a larger agreement later.
detection_hint: Does the flow lack any small "yes" moments before the final ask?
example_fix: Structure the form/quiz to elicit small agreements before the final ask.

name: Mirroring
description: Matching the customer's own language and tone increases rapport and persuasion.
detection_hint: Is the copy tone mismatched to how the target audience actually speaks?
example_fix: Adapt vocabulary and tone to match the target audience's own language.

name: Money Omission
description: Removing currency symbols/words from a price reduces the felt "pain of paying."
detection_hint: Is the currency symbol/word repeated heavily near the price?
example_fix: Test omitting the currency symbol in price display (e.g. "29" vs "CHF 29.00").

name: Moral Licensing
description: After acting virtuously, people feel licensed to indulge afterward.
detection_hint: Is there no indulgent upsell positioned after a "good" choice step?
example_fix: Position an indulgent add-on after a virtuous choice in the flow.

name: Pseudo Justifikation
description: People comply more readily when given any reason for a request, even a weak one.
detection_hint: Do requests/CTAs carry no stated reason at all?
example_fix: Add a brief "because" reason to key requests and CTAs.

name: Reaktanz
description: People resist when they feel their freedom of choice is being threatened.
detection_hint: Is the copy aggressive or pressuring in tone?
example_fix: Soften pressuring language and restore a visible sense of choice.

name: Reverse Psychology
description: Suggesting the opposite of the desired action can increase compliance in reactance-prone moments.
detection_hint: Not typically detectable as an absence; a niche, situational pattern.
example_fix: Use sparingly, only where reactance is clearly present (e.g. "not for everyone" framing).

name: Reziprozitaet
description: People feel obligated to return value or favors given to them.
detection_hint: Is there no free value offered before the ask (content, tool, sample)?
example_fix: Offer something genuinely useful for free before asking for the sale.

name: That's-Not-All-Technik
description: Adding a bonus before the customer can respond increases the offer's perceived value.
detection_hint: Is the offer a single flat price with no added bonus revealed?
example_fix: Add a small bonus to the offer before presenting the final price.

name: Unity
description: Emphasizing shared identity or group membership increases persuasion.
detection_hint: Is there no "we"/community framing anywhere in the copy?
example_fix: Use "join the community" framing rather than purely transactional language.

name: Zeitinkonsistenz
description: Preferences shift depending on how far away in time the decision or reward is.
detection_hint: Is there no differentiation between short-term and long-term commitment framing?
example_fix: Offer flexible commitment lengths that match different time preferences.

name: Anticipated Regret
description: The fear of future regret motivates people to act now.
detection_hint: Is there no honest framing of the regret from inaction?
example_fix: Add copy addressing the real cost of missing out, without exaggeration.

name: Autonomy Bias
description: People prefer options that preserve their sense of control and choice.
detection_hint: Is the flow a single forced path with no meaningful options?
example_fix: Offer a small, meaningful (not overwhelming) choice within the flow.

name: Cognitive Ease
description: Information that is easier to process feels more true and trustworthy.
detection_hint: Is the copy dense or the layout complex and hard to scan?
example_fix: Simplify language, increase whitespace, use a familiar, readable layout.

name: Decision Fatigue
description: Decision quality declines the more decisions a person has already made.
detection_hint: Are there many choices required late in the checkout flow?
example_fix: Reduce the number of choices/steps required near the end of checkout.

name: Halo Effect
description: One strong positive trait causes broader positive assumptions about the whole.
detection_hint: Is there no single strong credibility signal (award, notable client) shown early?
example_fix: Lead with one strong credibility signal to positively color the overall impression.

name: Hick's Law
description: The time to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices.
detection_hint: Are there too many navigation or CTA options on one screen?
example_fix: Reduce the number of choices/CTAs presented on each screen.

name: Hobson's +1 Choice Effect
description: Framing a single recommended option as the straightforward choice can simplify decisions.
detection_hint: Not typically an absence; a niche pattern for very simple offers.
example_fix: Use only where a genuine single recommended path exists, framed clearly as such.

name: Loss Aversion
description: Losses are felt roughly twice as strongly as equivalent gains.
detection_hint: Are benefits framed only as gains, never as losses avoided?
example_fix: Reframe some benefit copy as "avoid losing X" rather than only "gain X."

name: Mental Accounting
description: People categorize money into separate mental "accounts" rather than treating it as fully fungible.
detection_hint: Is cost shown with no tie to a specific budget category the user already has?
example_fix: Frame cost against a specific existing budget category (e.g. "less than your coffee spend").

name: Priming
description: Prior exposure to a stimulus influences later judgments and behavior.
detection_hint: Is there no relevant priming imagery or wording placed before the ask?
example_fix: Introduce imagery/words earlier in the flow that prime the desired association.

name: Scarcity
description: Limited availability increases perceived value and urgency.
detection_hint: Are there no genuine stock, slot, or time-limit signals shown?
example_fix: Show real scarcity signals (stock level, deadline) only where genuinely true.

name: Self-Benefit
description: Explicitly tying the offer to the user's personal benefit increases motivation.
detection_hint: Is the benefit framed abstractly or for others, not the visitor directly?
example_fix: Rewrite benefit copy in second person, tied to the user's specific outcome.

name: Diderot Effect
description: Acquiring one item increases desire for complementary items that match it.
detection_hint: Is there no complementary product shown after purchase?
example_fix: Show complementary products that "complete the set" post-purchase.

name: Low Ball Effect
description: Securing commitment on favorable terms, then adjusting them, still yields higher compliance than starting with real terms.
detection_hint: Ethically sensitive pattern — check whether pricing/terms shift after initial commitment without clear disclosure.
example_fix: Ensure any change in price or terms after initial commitment is disclosed immediately and clearly, never exploited.

name: Action Bias
description: People prefer doing something over doing nothing, even when inaction would be better.
detection_hint: Is there no clear single next action immediately after the decision is made?
example_fix: Give an unmistakable single next step right after commitment.

name: Cheering
description: Positive reinforcement or celebration after an action increases satisfaction and completion.
detection_hint: Is the confirmation screen flat and purely transactional?
example_fix: Add a small celebratory moment (visual/message) after purchase or signup.

name: Commitment and Consistency
description: People act consistently with commitments and statements they've already made.
detection_hint: Is an earlier micro-commitment not referenced at the point of final commitment?
example_fix: Reference the user's earlier stated preference or goal at the final ask.

name: Confirmation Bias
description: People favor information that confirms their existing beliefs.
detection_hint: Does the copy fail to open with something that confirms the visitor's likely existing belief or pain point?
example_fix: Open with a statement that confirms the visitor's existing belief or pain point.

name: Flow
description: A state of full engagement and absorption increases persistence through a task.
detection_hint: Is checkout interrupted by friction (CAPTCHA, forced account creation) that breaks concentration?
example_fix: Remove unnecessary interruptions from the checkout sequence.

name: Hindsight Bias
description: After an outcome is known, it is seen as having been predictable all along.
detection_hint: Not usually detectable pre-purchase; more relevant to retention messaging.
example_fix: Leverage in retention copy ("you knew this was the right choice").

name: Illusion of Control
description: People overestimate their control or influence over outcomes.
detection_hint: Is the process passive and opaque with no visible user control?
example_fix: Give visible controls or customization even where the outcome is largely fixed.

name: Motivating Uncertainty Effect
description: Uncertain, variable rewards can be more motivating than certain ones of the same average value.
detection_hint: Is the reward/loyalty structure fixed and entirely predictable?
example_fix: Consider a variable-reward element (surprise bonus) in loyalty or gamification design.

name: Overjustification Effect
description: Adding extrinsic rewards for an already intrinsically motivated action can reduce that motivation.
detection_hint: Relevant mainly to loyalty-program design; check for over-rewarding routine actions.
example_fix: Avoid over-rewarding actions users would already do anyway; reserve incentives for genuinely marginal actions.

name: Progressive Disclosure
description: Revealing information gradually, only as needed, reduces cognitive load.
detection_hint: Are all form fields or information shown at once regardless of relevance?
example_fix: Break long forms/information into progressive steps, showing fields only when relevant.

name: Response Efficacy
description: Belief that the recommended action will actually solve the problem increases willingness to act.
detection_hint: Is there no proof that the product actually delivers on the stated problem?
example_fix: Add proof (data, testimonial, guarantee) that the product delivers the promised outcome.

name: Self-Efficacy
description: Belief in one's own ability to successfully complete an action.
detection_hint: Does the process look complex with no reassurance of ease?
example_fix: Reassure users the process is easy and fast ("takes 2 minutes").

name: Buyer's Remorse
description: Post-purchase regret or anxiety that can lead to cancellation or return.
detection_hint: Is there no reassurance messaging immediately after purchase?
example_fix: Send a reassuring confirmation message reinforcing that the decision was sound.

name: Cognitive Dissonance
description: Discomfort from conflicting beliefs or actions, resolved by rationalizing the choice made.
detection_hint: Is there no reinforcing messaging after purchase to help resolve any doubt?
example_fix: Reinforce the positive reasons for the choice in post-purchase communication.

name: Endowment Effect
description: People value things more once they own or possess them.
detection_hint: Is there no trial-ownership period offered before final commitment?
example_fix: Offer a trial period so users experience ownership before committing fully.

name: Inequity Aversion
description: People are sensitive to unfairness, both to themselves and to others.
detection_hint: Do existing customers get visibly worse deals than new customers, unacknowledged?
example_fix: Ensure existing customers aren't visibly worse off than new signups, or address the gap directly.

name: Labor Love Effect
description: People value things more when they've invested effort into creating or configuring them.
detection_hint: Is there no customization or configuration step offered?
example_fix: Add a configuration or personalization step that requires some user effort.

name: Pain-of-Paying Principle
description: The psychological discomfort of paying is reduced when payment is decoupled from consumption.
detection_hint: Is the payment moment tightly coupled to the consumption moment, maximizing felt pain?
example_fix: Decouple payment timing from usage where possible (subscriptions, saved payment methods).

name: Peak-End Rule
description: Experiences are judged mainly by their peak moment and how they end, not the average.
detection_hint: Is the ending of checkout or onboarding weak or abrupt?
example_fix: Design a strong, positive peak moment and a clear, satisfying ending.

name: Post-Purchase Rationalization
description: People justify their purchases after the fact to reduce dissonance.
detection_hint: Is there no supporting content sent after purchase to reinforce the decision?
example_fix: Send post-purchase content that reinforces the value of the decision made.

name: Competition
description: Competitive framing against others increases engagement and motivation.
detection_hint: Is there no leaderboard or comparative element where one could be relevant?
example_fix: Add a light competitive or comparative element (progress vs. peers) where appropriate.

name: Endowed Progress Effect
description: People are more motivated to finish a task when they perceive they've already made some progress.
detection_hint: Does a progress bar start at 0% even when the user has completed preliminary steps?
example_fix: Start the progress bar partially filled to reflect steps already taken.

name: Fresh Start Effect
description: Temporal landmarks (new year, birthday, Monday) increase motivation to commit to new behaviors.
detection_hint: Is offer timing unrelated to any natural fresh-start moment?
example_fix: Time offers or messaging around natural fresh-start moments.

name: Mayfly Effect
description: Perceiving a trigger as fleeting causes an outsized, urgent reaction to it.
detection_hint: Is there no framing of the moment as short-lived where one genuinely exists?
example_fix: Use fleeting-moment framing only where a real time-bound trigger exists.

name: Privilege
description: Making customers feel specially selected or privileged increases loyalty.
detection_hint: Is treatment of all customers undifferentiated, with no exclusive or tiered elements?
example_fix: Add a sense of exclusive access or status for loyal customers (early access, special tier).

name: Sunk Cost Fallacy
description: People continue a behavior because of resources already invested, even when irrational.
detection_hint: Is time/effort already invested by the customer not referenced when prompting renewal?
example_fix: Reference the value or progress already invested when prompting renewal.
